part.text:
All 20 test suites pass, including the previously failing `std-test` path cases.

The fix, in `include/fmt/std.h`:
- Added a `path_type_` member to `formatter<std::filesystem::path, Char>` (include/fmt/std.h:107).
- The `parse` function now accepts `n` (native) and `g` (generic) presentation types alongside `?` (include/fmt/std.h:120-126).
- In `format`, on Windows the generic string (`p.generic_string<path::value_type>()`) is used when `{:g}` is specified, otherwise the native string; on POSIX native is used (identical to generic there) (include/fmt/std.h:131-139). This path string is also passed to `write_escaped_path` so `{:?}` composes correctly.
- `convert_path_payload` now returns the given payload unchanged when `Char` equals the path character type, so a generic wide payload isn't silently replaced by the native one (include/fmt/std.h:300-305).

So `fmt::format("{:n}", p)` prints `p.native()` and `fmt::format("{:g}", p)` prints `p.generic_string()` with forward slashes on Windows, matching the issue's proposal.
